source.kind: Local static serialized resource values; runtime normalization remains a host adaptation

limitations: Authored collision intervals are zero-based half-open. Normalized intervals are one-based inclusive after subtracting initial world interval only. This is an explicit host clock adaptation, not an observed runtime trace.
Local ActionFrame.MarginFrame is the actionable duration; outerFrameCount includes unused animation tail. Negative MarginFrame means landing/state transition controls recovery.
Multiple AttackDataIds with the same HitID are alternative hit zones/states; they must not all deal damage on one contact.

Gauge contexts retain exact IndexID values in attacks. IsGaugeTargetAuto uses 70% of attacker GaugeOwner on hits and 50% on common guard indices1/4, with integer truncation before actor gain factors. Raw65535 is preserved as source data, never awarded directly.
Captured cinematic/throw per-hit contacts use OtherCollisionKey CollisionType7 in their own authored action clock; these exact amounts must not be averaged.
Perfect parry strike/projectile rows99/100 are not yet assigned exact native response actions.
Automatic damage/gauge/timer inheritance, all collision Condition/KindFlag and action switch semantics are retained where possible, but are not exhaustively reconstructed.

timerStops are original zero-based half-open SwitchKey TIMER_STOP intervals in each named action clock. They pause the round timer independently from WorldKey world stops and do not by themselves freeze actor resources/AI clocks.
